title: Event log retention as an operational switching cost
text: Sehgal argues that an AI agent should be fundamentally defined by its append-only event log (the complete history of prompts, context retrievals, tool invocations, and user interventions) rather than by the runtime, model, or infrastructure executing it. Consequently, an important operational switching cost resides in log ownership: if an organization cannot export and replay this operational history, migrating an agent workflow to a replacement platform requires rebuilding its accumulated tuning and behavioral context from scratch. (The argument is adapted as an architectural pillar in Ismail's manuscript, S42).
qualification: Vendor-origin architectural argument and position paper by the founder of Omnara (an open-source agent command center), also delivered as an AI Engineer World's Fair keynote. Proposes treating append-only event logs as the persistent definition of an agent rather than models or runtime infrastructure. Retaining, redacting, and replaying extensive agent telemetry creates substantial data-governance, storage, and privacy overhead in enterprise settings.
